newsitem.title: USA: U.S. east seen cold next week - Smith Barney.
newsitem.headline: U.S. east seen cold next week - Smith Barney.

text.p: As many as three waves of cold Arctic air look likely to sweep into the U.S. east of the Rocky Mountains, U.S. beginning late next week, a closely-watched weather forecaster said.

"All indications point to an extended period of cold weather for much of the nation from the Rockies to the East Coast," Jon Davis, a forecaster with Smith Barney in Chicago, wrote in his daily report.
"This stretch of cold weather will begin next and likely continue through the end of the month," Davis said, noting the west will be the only region spared of the cold.

Davis said the first wave of cold weather will hit the upper midcontinent of the U.S. by early next week, preceded and/or accompanied by major stormy weather that will produce snowfall in the midcontinent, and as it spreads, thunderstorms in the South and heavy rainfall on the Eastern seaboard.
He said cold temperatures in the eastern third of the nation will average 12 to 18 degrees below normal by late next week including the weekend.
He said a second cold airmass similar to the first in trajectory will likely begin moving into the midcontinent during the week of December 23.
He said computer guidance indicates a third similar wave may sweep into the U.S. at the end of the month.
He noted possible precipitation associated with the second and third waves of cold is now too sketchy to reliably predict.
